comparison: Both address PSD findings (C3, C17, C18, C21, C22, C24, C50, C58). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with internally consistent data across preparation methods. Peer review is UNCERTAIN: Reviewer 1 finds PSD analysis 'not convincing' with 'forced comparison', while Reviewer 2 acknowledges 'significant' findings with rigorous quantification. Major disagreement on interpretation quality.

Perfect claim overlap (C37, C38, C39, C40, C60) on synaptic cleft measurements. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative consistency across methods and reasonable interpretation of shrinkage. Peer reviewers note 'unexpected variability' and view findings as updating previous measurements, with no challenges to the data.

Both address glutamate receptor distribution (C41-C48). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with comprehensive analysis including subtomogram averaging and independent validation. Peer review also SUPPORTED: reviewers acknowledge receptor identification and clustering as 'highly exciting' with no methodological challenges.

Peer reviewers mention 'polyhedral vesicles that have not been observed before' as a major discovery, with no challenges.
